summary: Iteration 59 – Phase 4 TxForm polish (specs #14/#15/#16/#17) verified on Expo web preview at 390x844 as alex+test1@jaleter.app. 6/7 numbered checks pass end-to-end. ONE FUNCTIONAL BUG found (P0 for spec #14): the running 'Allocated $X / $Y' and '$X left/over' status labels use the shared MONEY() helper from /app/frontend/src/quoteLibrary.ts which is defined as `(n) => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString('en-US')}`` — so integer-cent precision that Phase 4 restored INTERNALLY (splitsRemainingCents=20 for 48.80-20.50-28.55, etc.) is ROUNDED to whole dollars WHEN DISPLAYED. Reproduction: amount 48.80, splits 20.50 + 28.55 → real remainder is $0.25 OVER, but UI shows literally `$0 over` and `Allocated $49 / $49` (should show $48.80 / $48.80). The `Balanced` state at 20.25+28.55 works because remainder is truly 0. This defeats spec #14's user-visible promise (user can no longer see the cents delta they need to correct). Fix is a 1-line change: use a cent-precision formatter in the splits status block, e.g. `n => `$${n.toFixed(2)}`` when |n|<1 or always. Everything else in Phase 4 works: decimal-pad amount input keeps '4.75' verbatim, tx-category-open renders a single tappable row (no chip wall) that opens a searchable Sheet titled 'Select Category', typing 'Food' collapses the list to `tx-category-group-steward` + `tx-category-sub-food`, selection round-trips to `Steward · Food & Dining` on the picker row; tx-category-transfer round-trips to 'Transfer'; picking `tx-category-group-give` shows 'Give · Tithe'. Per-split side toggle: tapping `tx-split-0-side-income` correctly swaps row 0's group chips from give/steward/grow/enjoy → w2/contract/business while row 1 stays on the expense list. Refund income→expense flip saves without JS error (visual Budget netting not exercised — the test user has no budget with tracked subs). Navigation regression clean (home/budget/networth/legacy/transactions all OK, zero console errors, tx-filter still exactly [All | Income | Expenses]). Minor observation: `addSplit()` seeds TWO rows on the FIRST call because it always appends an empty row on top of the seed — so the spec's phrase 'tap Add split once so there are 2 rows' is a MIS-STATEMENT, actual behavior is 2 rows after `tx-split-toggle` alone, and tapping `tx-split-add` yields 3 rows. Not a bug per se but confusing UX (see action_items). Also, the spec test text 'row 0 = 20.50 → $0.20 left' is arithmetically wrong: 20.50 + 28.55 = 49.05, so remainder is -$0.25 (i.e. OVER by 25¢, not 20¢ LEFT). The direction shown in UI ('over') is therefore correct, only the precision is lost.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Allocated $X / $Y' and the '$X left / $X over' status text round to whole dollars because MONEY() at /app/frontend/src/quoteLibrary.ts:73 is `n => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString('en-US')}``. With amount=48.80 and splits 20.50+28.55, the UI shows `Allocated $49 / $49` and `$0 over` instead of `$48.80 / $48.80` and `$0.25 over`. This directly defeats the user-visible half of spec #14 — the internal integer-cent math is correct (splitsRemainingCents is exact) but the user cannot see the cents delta they need to reconcile. Also affects the disabled-Save error copy at index.tsx:3293 ('Splits must total exactly $49') and any other cents-sensitive line that calls MONEY(). Fix: introduce a cent-precision formatter (e.g. `centsFmt = (dollars) => `$${dollars.toFixed(2)}`) and use it in the splits status block at index.tsx:3235, 3240, 3242, 3293 (and any tight budget deltas).

issues: addSplit() at index.tsx:2953 seeds `tx.splits.length===0 ? 1 : 0` rows PLUS always appends one — so the very first tap of `tx-split-toggle` yields TWO rows, not one. The spec doc said 'a single row appears initially; tap Add split once so there are 2 rows' — with current code, tapping Add split at that point yields THREE rows. Either make the initial toggle yield 1 row (drop the trailing append when seeding) or update the copy so users know.

action_items: P0 (spec #14 fix): Replace `MONEY(splitsTotal)` / `MONEY(parsedAmount)` / `MONEY(splitsRemaining)` / `MONEY(-splitsRemaining)` at /app/frontend/app/index.tsx lines 3235, 3240, 3242 and the copy at 3293 with a cent-precision formatter (`v => `$${v.toFixed(2)}``). The integer-cent math is fine — this is purely a display regression from reusing the whole-dollar MONEY() helper. Otherwise Phase 4's core promise ('48.80 + 3.70 no longer drifts and the user CAN SEE it') is invisible to users.

P2 (UX polish, optional): Reduce addSplit()'s initial seed so `tx-split-toggle` opens exactly 1 empty split row rather than 2, so 'Add split once ⇒ 2 rows' matches the user's mental model. Trivial patch in addSplit at index.tsx:2953-2964: when tx.splits is empty, set `splits: [ { …one empty… } ]` and skip the trailing append.

P2 (test creds hygiene): The 'Verify your email' banner still shows for alex+test1 on every login even after 60+ iterations of use — consider auto-verifying seeded test users on backend (or dismiss the banner persistently) so QA screenshots aren't cluttered.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx:3097-3126 — Category picker single-row opener is clean and correctly renders `Tap to select` / `Steward · Food & Dining` / `Transfer` via a single IIFE. No chip wall regression.

index.tsx:3304-3401 — Category Sheet correctly filters by lowercase substring on both group and subcategory names; Transfer is anchored at the bottom with distinct styling. autoFocus on `tx-category-search` works on web.

index.tsx:3155-3180 — Per-split side toggle correctly re-seeds groupId/detailId from the correct list (incomeSources vs categories) when switching, so no dangling references to expense subs remain when a row is flipped to income.
index.tsx:2953-2964 — addSplit's `seed` logic double-appends on first call (creates 2 rows in one tap of tx-split-toggle). Not incorrect but confusing given the spec copy — recommend simplification.

index.tsx:3270-3286 — `preservedSign` fallback (`tx.type === 'income' ? 1 : -1`) is the right default for new manual rows; combined with `spentForSubInMonth`/`receivedForIncomeInMonth`'s sign-aware netting, Phase 4 spec #16 semantics are consistent.

quoteLibrary.ts:73 — MONEY() is used in ~40 places for high-level KPI display (Wealth, Reports, Budget summary) where whole-dollar rounding is fine. The regression is only that the splits status block reuses the SAME helper — introducing a `MONEY_CENTS` sibling is cleaner than mutating MONEY globally.
app/index.tsx remains ~5,419 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. TxForm alone is ~800 lines. Consider extracting to /app/frontend/src/screens/TxForm.tsx now that its API surface has stabilized.

success_rate.frontend: 6/7 numbered checks pass. The one HIGH-priority fail is the MONEY() rounding in the splits status labels (spec #14 display regression).

seed_data_creation: Created 3 test transactions locally during the run (Coffee shop $4.75 · Food & Dining; Split test $48.80 with 2 splits; Refund test $48.80 income→expense). These are stored client-side in localStorage and get wiped between browser sessions per Jaleter's manual-tx model.
context_for_next_testing_agent: TxForm entry point on Activity screen is the `+` circle button `tx-add` in the header (there is also `tx-empty-add` and `tx-empty-connect` when the list is empty). Sub id for 'Food & Dining' is literally `food` (so `tx-category-sub-food`, NOT `-food-dining` as the review request wrote). Split rows are `tx-split-{0..n-1}-amount|-side-income|-side-expense|-group-{gid}|-sub-{sid}|-remove`; `tx-split-add` and `tx-split-toggle` are the buttons. Note that `tx-split-toggle` alone creates 2 rows (addSplit's seed+append behavior); do NOT click `tx-split-add` after toggling unless you want 3 rows. To reopen an existing tx, click `tx-{txid}` (NOT `tx-row-{txid}`). MONEY() from /app/frontend/src/quoteLibrary.ts rounds to whole dollars — expect any UI text formatted with it to show `$49` instead of `$48.80`.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of the spec #14 display regression: TxForm at index.tsx:3235,3240,3242,3293 reuses the shared MONEY() helper from quoteLibrary.ts:73, which is `n => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString('en-US')}`` — designed for KPI cards where whole-dollar rounding is intentional. When TxForm was upgraded (Phase 4) to integer-cent internal math, the DISPLAY layer was not updated to a cent-precision formatter, so the UI silently truncates the very cents the internal math preserves. Mitigation: introduce a sibling `MONEY_CENTS(n) = `$${n.toFixed(2)}`` (or use `n.toLocaleString('en-US',{minimumFractionDigits:2, maximumFractionDigits:2})`) and swap it into the four call sites in the splits status block. All other MONEY() usages can stay whole-dollar.
